intro.text: Been a year on drones. From flight controllers to chassis to perception and positioning, it's been a long freaking year. Started with the wish of flying a drone hahaha n now im neck deep in obsession. I have made a lot of mistakes but learned a lot more sooo here goes nothing.
Note: im a broke college student in a really cool robotics club SRA.

runs.text: I started with a trainer kit and all i wanted was to fly it a little coz well its cool right?! Newsflash: it was a year old with hacky hardware. The transmitter had no working switches so i put the arm switch on an analog switch, not one of my brightest ideas.(and no the throttle stick arm wasnt working) Then I switched to a speedybee f4 stack and the esc board was cooked. Back to square one.
Uk how when someone says u cant do something and suddenly all u wanna do is that thing. Me being extremely immature, I have that. Now I really wanted to fly a damn drone.

My mentors were ready to buy me speedybee’s new fc but in India it was out of stock everywhere (only on the sites I knew then, I could've found other fcs, obviously I realise that now). Waiting was pure torture for someone as impatient as me.

Buried in exams and impatience, I got asked why I am not making my own. So I did. I learned pcb designing and spent a month and half on my first fc. It lacked thorough research on power management and had a couple of design flaws, but it was something. I had started directly with an stm32 and made the whole rx tx and everything. I was told to start smaller. Guess who didn't listen? That's right, me. But going big helped(not with the money), coz it meant mistakes were louder.
The second one was a smaller esp32 fc over wifi, with coreless motors instead of BLDCs. I pitched it and my juniors took it from there.. It kinda works… (havent found the right battery yet).
https://github.com/Aryan2804/Icarus
Meanwhile the fc (NovaF4) i ordered showed up, so ofc i 3d printed frames n kept trying to fly.
Betaflight configurator and Ardupilot have so many parameters. Debugging why anything won't work needs time, time and patience.
Then those flew. But the obsession wasn't just flying anymore. It was the whole process. I fell in love with it.
It's hard to show what i did coz how do u show the hours of soldering, 3D printing, taping only to have another wire or part broken. But where right?

All this and then I noticed I'm not good at flying at all. I kept thinking what if someone really wants this like me and still can't fly? I dont have fast enough reflexes yet. What if I just wanna prompt and get it to fly, what then? So now I had another direction: making drones smart.
Now the thing with hacky hardware is it has its limits. I needed to build a proper setup for this which is hard considering i didnt have money backing. Que in my mentor again…
My mentor told me to apply for grants. I did, with a lot of pushing. After a long month of interviews and forms and rejections, finally
GradCapital
did it for me.

I wanted a crazyflie…drumroll pls… out of stock, and this time i did check all sites. So I bought a betafpv air75 whoop. Not the best choice for rl or vio tbh, but remember how I like to do what I'm told I can't.
RAPTOR

paper: one recurrent neural network policy that can fly almost any quadrotor, from 31 g to 2.4 kg, with no tuning….. really cool paper. I wanted it on the air75, running on the drone itself inside betaflight, 100 times a second.
A lot went wrong:
Size.
The pretraining range was 31 g to 2.4 kg n my whoop is 35 to 45 g, a pretty edge case. So I retrained for whoop size.
Position.

The policy needs position and velocity and the air75 has nothing for that. So the laptop does the vision and sends position up to the drone through my radio. First I tried an external camera tracking an AruCo on the drone (flight space too small), then visual slam (fpv cam not that great).

What finally worked, after being stuck for ages, was AruCo markers stuck on the walls: the program knows where every marker corner is not solved for where the camera must be. Blur from analog video meant only 30 to 58% of frames gave a position, so I added optical flow to fill the gaps (87 to 100% coverage, about 1 cm median error).
Delay.

The video is about 112 ms late, so positions reach the policy 140 to 160 ms old. Plain retraining with delay failed (86 to 92% of sim flights crashed). What worked was making the drone predict, pushing each old position forward using its accelerometer, and training in a nastier sim with real noise and dropped frames. Crashes in sim went down to about 5%.
Takeoff and landing.

Tell the policy to go to 30 cm while it's on the floor and it launches at 1 m/s coz the floor wont let it move. So the target rises gently, and for landing it sinks below the floor. The landing bounced for ages until I found the laptop's height correction was still lifting the floor target. Of course.

Over three days (21 to 23 oct) I flew about 25 to 30 flights. The good ones took off, held a point, flew a circle and landed by themselves. Hover error was 12 to 17 cm over a whole hold, and circles tracked within 9 to 16 cm.

Now ud think itll all work out right. Yes n no. Yes coz it kinda works. No coz after all these tests n broken runs the air75 is roughened up, one motor is faulty n the flashing port isnt working now…hahaha.
The drones own fpv camera as a position sensor worked better than expected, up to the limits of analog video. So yeah, worth everything.

sections.title: Crazyflie: a room, 5 distance sensors, one tiny drone

runs.text: One drone gone and I was upset, it had been months since I was drone-less. Luckily god likes me quite a fair bit, my crazyflie arrived two days later. It's soo freaking adorable hahaha.

But obviously strings attached, i didnt get a flow deck. I only have the multiranger deck: 5 lasers (front, back, left, right, up). No flow deck, no mocap. So the question became: can a 27 g drone map a room, find where it is and avoid obstacles with just those? (I tried a camera first. It browned out on the drones battery, so vision waits for a regulator.)
Position from walls.

x from the front or back wall, y from the right wall, height from the ceiling. First hover was within ±4 to 5 cm. Then came the fun: front and back readings disagreed, a beam crossing a box edge made the position teleport, and my fix for that hid a real drift when the drone hit the wall. The fix for the fix: only trust a jump if the opposite beam agrees.
Mapping.
Lawnmower sweeps build a map, one per height, coz a room isn't the same at every height.
Where am I?

A particle filter finds its position from scratch in 0.3 s. Letting it steer directly failed (too slow, ±25 cm wobble). So the walls steer and the filter is a referee that steps in only when a wall reading looks off.
Avoiding stuff.

It plans a route, marks anything the beams see that isn't in the map, and re-plans every 2 s. It flew around a box it had never seen, passed through a gap of about 60 cm, and mapped the box as it went. It avoids obstacles (mainly me) pretty nicely.
Crashes (best part).
Every crash got replayed in sim n turned into a new safety check. It also lands if I hit Ctrl+C and cuts the motors at once if I hit Ctrl+\.

Then ported RAPTOR on it too. It runs on wall position instead of mocap, PID handles takeoff and landing, and it falls back to PID within 0.2 s if the laptop stops engaging. Hover held within a median of 4.2 cm sideways and 2.5 cm in height. The figure eight with changing height tracked within about 8 to 10 cm median, max around 20 cm. One catch: it hovers at about 73% thrust vs 63% for PID, so there's little headroom for aggressive moves.

With few sensors, knowing when to distrust a sensor matters more than the planner. Replay every crash log in sim before flying again. And the hours of printing, taping, fixing, soldering and desoldering don't show up in a repo, but the flights do.

So if u r someone who thinks it wont work out coz u dont have the right hardware or u think all those debugging hours aren't showing up, trust me they will. Took me a year to finally have flying drones but here I am. Lastly,
Dear drones, thank you for ruining my sanity, my wallet and my free time. I would do it all over again.
